title: UPS Runtime Reduction Drives Battery Technology Shift in Data Centers
snippet: Tod Higinbotham, COO of ZincFive, explores the race to reduce uninterruptible power supply (UPS) runtimes.
description: ZincFive COO explores how faster generator failover enables sub-5-minute UPS runtimes, challenging lead-acid and lithium-ion battery economics and footprint.
so_what: Runtime compression from 30min to 3min forces battery oversizing with lead-acid/lithium due to discharge rate and thermal runaway limits, consuming revenue floor space.
summary: Tod Higinbotham of ZincFive examines the trend toward sub-5-minute and 3-minute UPS runtimes enabled by faster generator failover. Traditional lead-acid batteries lack power density for short bursts, while lithium-ion BMS safety shutdowns at high discharge rates cripple systems during outages, forcing costly battery bank oversizing.
why_it_matters: Data center operators moving from 30-minute to 3-minute UPS runtimes face a constraint: lead-acid's low energy density requires more cabinets, and lithium-ion BMS shutdowns during high-discharge events create reliability gaps. This forces oversizing battery banks, consuming valuable floor space that could house revenue-generating servers and increasing upfront capital costs.
